PagerDuty: INCIDENT: P0 - multiple gpu nodes reporting "kernel reset" and kubelet restarts, elevated error rate on /v1/generate (start=3098765432) :rotating_light:
InfraBot: alerts: gpu-node-*-kernel-reset x5 in 3m, pods restarting (image: rwd-inference/serve:v2), autoscaler scaled up 12 -> 36 in last 4m, then scaled down to 8 in 2m (metric: gpu_util spikes)
Maya (oncall): I'm on it. pulling logs now. @Tony @Sam FYI.
Maya (oncall): quick customer impact: ~18% 5xx on hosted, spikes to 40% tail for large-model routes. Support page flagged.
Tony (eng-runtime): initial guess: GPU driver/kernel panic (nvidia: GPU reset), devices disappearing -> container failures. Could be a bad kernel module or a model causing pathological memory patterns.
Sam (sre): autoscaler behaviour looks bad — it's oscillating. scale-up on spike then some nodes get kernel-reset -> pods reattached -> scheduler reschedules -> more spikes. We have a feedback loop.
Alex (support): getting customer reports about timeouts and degraded throughput. CS alerted enterprise customers and opened tickets.
Maya (oncall): commands I'm running:```
# list node events
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu
kubectl describe node gpu-az3-12 | tail -n 50
journalctl -u kubelet -n 200
```
Maya (oncall): node events show repeated "container runtime got signal SIGSEGV" and "NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus"
Helga (infra): that matches NVidia driver/kernel resets. We upgraded driver image last week on some hosts. Rolling driver drift could explain subset of nodes failing.
Tony (eng-runtime): mitigation proposal: 1) pause cluster autoscaler to stop oscillation, 2) cordon and drain the nodes showing kernel resets, 3) pin serving pods to a stable node pool without the new driver (nodeSelector), 4) revert driver on affected nodes or reboot into previous AMI.
Sam (sre): +1 to pause autoscaler. We need to avoid automated scale-down that evicts healthy pods and creates more scheduling churn.
Maya (oncall): I'm pausing the autoscaler now: `kubectl scale deployment cluster-autoscaler --replicas=0 -n kube-system` -> completed.
InfraBot: cluster-autoscaler scaled to 0 replicas by Maya (oncall). Reaction: :white_check_mark:
Maya (oncall): cordoning gpu-az3-12 and gpu-az3-14 now. `kubectl cordon gpu-az3-12` -> success.
Maya (oncall): draining gpu-az3-12 with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to force pods off. Some pods fail to start on other nodes because they request specific GPU types.
Tony (eng-runtime): temporary change: update Deployment nodeAffinity to prefer older-driver nodepool and reduce maxConcurrentRestarts:```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: rwd-serve}
spec:
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 10%
      maxSurge: 0
  template:
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
            - matchExpressions:
              - key: nodepool
                operator: In
                values:
                - gpu-stable-old-driver
```
Maya (oncall): applying the affinity patch to the two biggest serving deployments.
Maya (oncall): after affinity change, successful scheduling onto stable pool. 5xx rate dropping to ~6% now.
Sam (sre): we're seeing kernel resets limited to nodes in latest-driver pool. Good sign. Need to prevent autoscaler from putting new pods on that pool.
Helga (infra): ordering emergency rollback of driver to previous AMI for affected AZ. Rolling reboot plan: cordon -> drain -> replace -> uncordon. Starting with gpu-az3-12.
Tony (eng-runtime): also lowering pod resource limits for large-model routes to reduce chance of device OOMs while we stabilize. Patch pushed.
Maya (oncall): note: some pods had restart loops because they failed init with "cuda: device lost" then crashed quickly; changed livenessProbe initialDelaySeconds to 45s to avoid flapping.
Maya (oncall): timeline so far: alert 3098765432, autoscaler paused 3098765450, affinity patch applied 3098765462, kernel-rollback initiated 3098765478.
OpsLead: customer communications: draft posted to #product-status, will publish status page message: "Degraded performance for text-generation routes; mitigation in progress."
Alex (support): opened high-priority tickets for top 5 enterprise customers, assigning to SEs for direct updates.
Sam (sre): remaining tasks: 1) keep autoscaler paused until driver rollback completes and we see 15m stable, 2) monitor pod restart count and 5xx rate, 3) run canary traffic on stable pool to validate.
Tony (eng-runtime): follow-up: we should add a safety gating rule to autoscaler that avoids scaling to nodepools with driverVersion != cluster-stable-driver for 24h after a driver rollout. Filing tech debt ticket.

Helga (infra): node gpu-az3-12 replaced, uncordoned. Rebooted into old AMI. Observability: no kernel-reset events on that node after reboot (+10m).
Maya (oncall): 5xx at 1.2% now, request latency returned to normal p50/p95. Restarts dropping.
PagerDuty: Incident status: mitigated — customer impact reduced; monitoring.
Maya (oncall): I'm handing to Sam for postmortem. Sam, can you take lead?
Sam (sre): I'll run the postmortem, collecting kernel logs, driver rollout timeline, and autoscaler events. Initial blame: coupling driver rollout with autoscaler scale events, and missing gating rule allowed autoscaler to accelerate churn. Also need better device-failure isolation for pods (don't schedule critical routes onto nodes in rollout pool).
Maya (oncall): closing the pager but keeping thread open for follow-ups. Thanks everyone :tada:
